note: Hand corrections to the English Wikipedia article a record links to, applied by tools/link_fixes.py (also called by build_region.py, so a rebuild keeps them). A polity's link comes from Cliopatria's Wikipedia column, an event's from its Wikidata enwiki sitelink; where that leads to a disambiguation page, the modern place, a person or a redirect into a longer article, the record gets the article (and section) about it. Every entry says why. Found while translating the summaries (data/README.md, Changes, 26 October 2026). Checked against English Wikipedia on 26 October 2026.

angevins.why: Angevin is a disambiguation page; the record (1126–1146, France) is the county the Angevins ruled.

bali.why: Bali is the modern island and province; the record (1687–1907) is the Balinese kingdoms.

kingdom-of-thuringia.why: Basina of Thuringia is a queen; the Thuringi article covers their kingdom (to 531).

county-of-berga.why: Berga is the modern town; there is no article on the county, the one on its counts covers it.

danish-magnates.why: The record (1333–1351) sits in the Estonia column, which Denmark ruled until 1346; Christopher II is a king.

dongye.why: Dongye is a disambiguation page; Eastern Ye (Dongye) is the Korean chiefdom.

georgia-1918.why: Georgia is a disambiguation page; 1918–1921 is the Democratic Republic.

georgia-567.why: Georgia is a disambiguation page; in 567–576 the Georgian kingdom was Iberia (Kartli), abolished in 580.

turk-shahis.why: Kabul Shahi is a disambiguation page.

later-han.why: Later Han is a disambiguation page; the record is 947–959.

livonian-conference.why: The record is the Livonian Confederation (1422–1563), a section of Terra Mariana; Livonian language is the language.

mongol-khanate.why: Mongol khanate is a disambiguation page; the Mongol state of 1468–1635 is the Northern Yuan.

omani-slave-coast.why: Omanis is the article on the people; the record (1814–1855, Somalia and Tanzania) is the Omani Empire's East African coast.

county-of-pallars-jussa.why: Pallars Jussà is the modern comarca.

county-of-pallars-sobira.why: Pallars Sobirà is the modern comarca.

portuguese-africa.why: Portuguese Africa is a disambiguation page; the record (1507–1581) covers Cape Verde, São Tomé and Bioko, for which the Portuguese Empire is the common article.

southern-wu.why: Southern Wu is a disambiguation page; Yang Wu, also called Southern Wu, is the Ten Kingdoms state.

strathclyde.why: Strathclyde is the modern council region.

sultanate-of-perak.why: Sultan of Perak is the modern office; the sultanate has a section in History of Malaysia.

sultanate-of-selangor.why: Sultan of Selangor is the modern office; Selangor Sultanate redirects to this section.

xia.why: Xia is a disambiguation page; the record (410–438) is the Sixteen Kingdoms Xia (Hu Xia).

accepted.duchy-of-wroclaw: Duchy of Wrocław redirects to Duchy of Silesia, which covers the duchy of Wrocław; no article of its own.
accepted.free-city-of-frankfurt: The article covers the free city of 1815–1866 as well as the imperial city before it.
accepted.earldom-of-desmond: Earldom of Desmond redirects to Earl of Desmond; no article on the earldom.

unresolved.georgia-724: Georgia (724–1009, Georgia and Azerbaijan columns) is linked to a disambiguation page; no single article fits (the Principality of Iberia, Kakheti, Hereti and Abkhazia overlap these years).
unresolved.turks: Turks (666–756, Central Asia and China) is linked to a disambiguation page and to Wikidata's Oghuz Khagan; neither the Western nor the Second Turkic Khaganate matches the years.
unresolved.kapisa: Kapisa (1475–1506, Afghanistan) is linked to a disambiguation page; its Kingdom of Kapisa is of the 1st millennium.
unresolved.malaya: Malaya (1294–1351, Malaysia and Singapore) is linked to a disambiguation page; the Melayu Kingdom lay in Sumatra.
unresolved.norse: Norse (161–499, Denmark and Norway) is linked to a disambiguation page; the Norsemen article is about the Viking Age.
unresolved.breton-kingdoms: Breton Kingdoms (587–824) is linked to the article on the Bretons; the kingdoms (Domnonée, Cornouaille, Bro Waroch) have separate articles and none covers all.
unresolved.kastamonu: Kastamonu (1305–1343) is linked to the modern city; the beylik is either the Chobanids (to 1309) or the Candar dynasty (from about 1309), which the record's years straddle.
unresolved.kannauj-varman-dynasty: Kannauj-Varman Dynasty (732–771) is linked to the modern city; there is no article on the dynasty, only on Yashovarman.
unresolved.kelantan: Kelantan (1762–1904) is linked to the modern state; Kelantan Sultanate redirects to the modern office.
unresolved.negeri-sembilan: Negeri Sembilan (1775–1894) is linked to the modern state; no article on the historical confederacy.
unresolved.kedah-perlis-district: Kedah-Perlis District (1842–1910) is linked to the modern state of Perlis; no article on the district.
unresolved.sultanate-of-terengganu: Terengganu Sultanate redirects to the modern office (Sultan of Terengganu); History of Malaysia has no section on it.
unresolved.kingdom-of-pajana: Kingdom of Pajana (1572–1587) is linked to the Lontara script; no English article on the kingdom was found.
